American Board of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation (ABPMR) Pain Medicine subspecialty certification
American Board of Psychiatry and Neurology (ABPN) Pain Medicine subspecialty certification
boardStatus: Pain Medicine is an interdisciplinary subspecialty with shared examination standards. ABA offers the exam and publishes a 200-item blueprint with General (50%) and Clinical States (50%) domains. ABPMR and ABPN credential eligible diplomates through their own board pathways; ABA administers/develops the shared examination. No separate Pediatric Pain Medicine board exam or pediatric-only board certification was identified in the official sources checked. The BCH ACGME fellowship is an ACGME Pain Medicine fellowship with pediatric focus and adult rotations, not a distinct pediatric board. BCH also describes a separate non-ACGME 3–12 month educational option. Pediatricians are not thereby made pain-medicine board eligible: ABPN requirements specify neurology/child neurology/psychiatry diplomates; ABPMR requires ABPMR diplomate status; ABA requirements must be verified directly for the candidate’s primary board. ACGME eligibility is not equivalent to board eligibility.
boardEligibilityNotice: This independent course confers no eligibility. Candidate must independently verify current primary-board certification, approved prior residency, program-specific eligibility and examination requirements with the relevant board and fellowship director before applying. Eligibility and board rules checked 2026-10-07; requirements may change.

boardStatus: This is an actual pediatric physician subspecialty fellowship, not a generic directory label or research-only position. Johns Hopkins’ official program page identifies a 3-year ACGME-accredited Pediatric Pulmonary Fellowship. ABP publishes a separate Pediatric Pulmonology subspecialty certifying examination and a 19-domain blueprint effective for exams on/after 2026-11-01. The Hopkins page says select PhD applicants may be considered for postdoctoral work; that supplement is not physician fellowship/board training. No combined program is listed in the packet or verified. Alternative AOBP-specific certification routes were outside this packet and were not independently assessed.
boardEligibilityNotice: This self-study course conveys no ABP eligibility. ABP requires three years full-time fellowship in an ACGME/RCPSC-accredited Pediatric Pulmonology program, prior General Pediatrics certification maintained as applicable, unrestricted license, director verification, scholarly activity requirements and passing the subspecialty exam. Confirm latest rules directly with ABP; institutional PhD postdoctoral consideration is not physician certification eligibility.

boardEligibilityNotice: Self-study confers no board eligibility. As checked 2026-10-07, the ABS requires accredited 2-year pediatric-surgery training, general-surgery certification, unrestricted licensure requirements as specified, and other current application rules; applicants must re-check ABS policies at application. The ABS PSQE/PSCE are required for initial pediatric surgery certification. This educational course cannot satisfy any training, case log, PALS, licensure or eligibility requirement. [R6-R10]

boardStatus: Boston Children’s Hospital names the Alan B. Retik Pediatric Urology Fellowship as a two-year ACGME-accredited physician fellowship. ABU maintains a distinct Pediatric Urology subspecialty certification and exam; it is not a separate entry-level primary specialty board. No other institution or combined fellowship track is claimed in this item. ABU’s 2026 public page states the PSCE is offered every other year and lists October 22–24, 2026; as of the 2026-10-07 check, this is forthcoming. The 2026 ABU detailed content page was blocked by a cookie challenge; no question weighting is asserted. ABU describes broad examination content, including congenital abnormalities, childhood-acquired urologic problems and adolescent overlap.
boardEligibilityNotice: Not eligible for board certification by completing this independent course. ABU states candidates must hold a current unrestricted general ABU urology certificate, practice pediatric urology, complete at least 24 months in an approved pediatric urology program, meet practice/log/CME requirements and pass its examination. Current 2026 requirements may change; the ABU candidate handbook is the controlling source. Never interpret this notice as individualized eligibility advice.
